title: Commodities Brief — 12 May 2026

sections.heading: COMMODITIES BRIEF
sections.content:
12 May 2026 • 06:11 CET

Headline: Commodities Markets — Session Overview

Commodities rally continues amid weakening dollar and mounting supercycle evidence. Risk-on sentiment supports industrial metals while agricultural complex gains on supply concerns. Real rates remain supportive for precious metals complex.

sections.heading: Precious Metals
sections.content: Gold consolidates at $4717.20/oz (-0.03% intraday), finding support from negative real yields and central bank diversification flows. Silver outperforms at $85.96/oz (+0.55%), benefiting from industrial demand recovery. Platinum weakens to $2097.80/oz (-0.84%) on automotive sector headwinds, while palladium retreats to $1503.50/oz amid supply normalization. Copper surges to $6.49/lb (+1.23%), confirming global growth acceleration thesis.

sections.heading: Energy
sections.content: Oil complex extends gains with WTI at $99.40/bbl (+1.36%) and Brent at $105.29/bbl (+1.04%) on tightening fundamentals. OPEC+ production discipline and geopolitical premium support higher prices. Brent-WTI spread widens to $5.89/bbl reflecting refining capacity constraints. Natural gas climbs to $2.93/MMBtu (+0.69%) on storage deficit concerns.

sections.heading: Agriculture
sections.content: Grains rally sharply with wheat leading at $641.50/bu (+3.09%) on European drought concerns. Corn advances to $474.50/bu (+2.98%) while soybeans reach $1214.25/bu (+1.21%) as La Nina weather patterns threaten South American crops.

sections.heading: Trade Ideas
sections.content:
LONG: Silver (industrial demand recovery), Wheat (weather premium), Copper (supercycle acceleration)
SHORT/HEDGE: Palladium (oversupply), Long-dated WTI puts (demand destruction risk)

sections.heading: Key Risks
sections.content: Federal Reserve pivot toward aggressive tightening could reverse dollar weakness. Chinese property sector deterioration threatens industrial metals demand. Escalating Middle East tensions present upside energy risk.
